short: Closed-loop sentence voice from intracortical arrays holds for one participant; the design is standard, forced-choice and proxy-target metrics overstate intelligibility.
position: The paper [@wairagkar2025] changed the training targets (M02, TTS audio aligned to neurally inferred boundaries), the decoder (M06, causal closed-loop synthesis) and the output (M08, voice with intonation and pitch). All three are standard: closed-loop synthesis existed for vowels and unintelligible words, and all results are from one participant. The main claim holds: sentence-level voice from intracortical signals, heard as the user attempts to speak, with acoustic leakage ruled out. Intelligibility is weaker than the headline: 94.34% six-choice matching (chance about 17%, inference) sits beside a 43.75% median open-transcription WER that the authors also report (Fig. 2l). The same group's [later] causal model reaches 5.24% listener WER on this paper's benchmark, offline with simulated real-time inference [@wairagkar2026], so this paper is the closed-loop proof, not the quality benchmark.
